newsitem.title: INDIA: Sharp world lows scuttle Indian gold prices. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sharp world lows scuttle Indian gold prices. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]

text.p: ** Indian 24 carat gold prices on Friday fall by 30 rupees
at 4,370 rupees in opening trade and panic selling (corrects from buying)
triggered by fresh losses in the world market
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) starts 400
rupees lower at 51,100 rupees after losing 400 rupees on
** Silver (.999) opens 75 rupees lower at 6,550 rupees per
kg on higher inflows and sliding world prices.
Indian 24 carat gold prices on Friday opened 30 rupees lower at 4,370 rupees per 10 grammes in panic selling (corrects from buying) triggered by fresh world market lows, dealers said.
Gold was down by 35 rupees per 10 grammes on Thursday.
"There is panic among local traders due to a fresh fall in world prices," one broker said.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) opened 400 rupees lower at 51,100 rupees, falling by a similar margin on Thursday.
"They may fall below the 51,000 rupees mark, and looking at the sharp losses in the world market biscuit prices may fall to the 50,000 rupees mark," he said.
Silver (.999) opened 75 rupees lower at 6,550 rupees per kg on higher arrivals and world market trends. Silver was up by five rupees per kg on Thursday.
